notes: New Recite tab: recite a whole Surah or a whole Mushaf page without stopping. The AI teacher listens to all of it, then shows every correction Ayah by Ayah. One recitation = one check, however long.
Up to a whole Surah (even Al-Baqarah) and up to an hour in one recitation.
Challenges moved to the Today screen.

Recite a whole section to the AI teacher — as many Ayahs as you like (up to 60) in one go, pausing as you normally would. It counts as just one check. Find it in the Revise tab and on every Surah page.
Much faster: the teacher now listens while you recite, so your results come within a few seconds of tapping I’m done.
Works in normal rooms: the phone’s noise suppression is on and the teacher skips background sounds and other noises.

Fairer for non-Arab accents: small pronunciation and harakah points are shown as tips (not counted), Madd lengths allow a count either way, and only missed or wrong words count against your memorisation. Tap “Not a mistake” if you disagree. Want it stricter? Me → Strict Tajweed checking.
Share button (Today and Me): send Hifz Academy to family and friends on WhatsApp or anywhere — with the Android download and the iPhone link.
Fair use for the AI teacher: each phone gets a daily allowance, and the owner’s family (with the family code, in Me) always comes first.
If the AI teacher’s allowance is used up, you’re told clearly and can still mark your own mistakes.
After you recite, every mistake now says exactly what was wrong: the word you missed, or what you said instead.
Correct it with the reciter: tap 🔊 next to any wrong word to hear it recited correctly, play the whole Ayah from your Qari, then Try again.
When the phone can’t judge clearly, it now shows what it heard.

AI recitation teacher: tap Recite to me and the teacher listens to your Ayah and points out missed or wrong words and letters, wrong harakat, and Tajweed mistakes — Madd lengths (with the counts you held), Ghunnah, Qalqalah and Idgham — each shown on its word with how to fix it.
Mistake colours: red = word or letter, purple = harakah, orange outline = Tajweed.
The teacher is an AI and can make mistakes: it helps you practise but does not replace a qualified teacher.
Fixed: tapping a Juz in the Quran journey showed a blank page. It now opens a list of that Juz’s Surahs with your progress in each.
New: How to use Hifz Academy — a 1-minute tour of every feature, with “Try it now” buttons (Today tab and Me tab).
New: Demo mode — explore the app with sample progress (Surahs memorised, a 12-day streak, revisions due). Your own progress is kept safe and comes back when you exit.
Recite to me 🎤: recite an Ayah aloud and the app marks any missed or wrong words in red (words only, not Tajweed). If it can’t hear clearly, it says so instead of guessing.
What does it mean? A short explanation of every Ayah (Al-Mukhtasar) in Malayalam, English or Arabic, in lessons and the Quran reader.
Kids mode: brighter colours, bigger text, Noor the friendly star, a sticker for every Ayah memorised, cheerful sounds and gentle break reminders.
Sound effects for correct answers and celebrations (can be turned off in Me).
A new app icon: the gold Rub el Hizb star with an open Mushaf, so it no longer looks like Family Budget.
Listen to 12 world-famous reciters, including two teaching-style recitations for memorising.
Read translations under every Ayah: Saheeh International, Hilali & Khan, Wahiduddin Khan, transliteration and two Malayalam translations.
Pick several goals and translations at once in setup.
A daily goal ring, streak week, levels, 15 badges and a Quran journey map.
Celebrations when you memorise an Ayah.
This Update button: new versions now install from inside the app.
Verified Quran text, 7-step memorisation lessons, spaced revision, challenges and streaks.
